blueprint.title: Release ETL Normalizer Accuracy Fix
blueprint.scenario: You are a release engineer on a data platform team. The nightly build ships a compiled C binary `/app/bin/etl_normalize` that ingests raw transaction CSV files, applies a multi-step normalization pipeline, and writes results to a SQLite database. The pipeline then runs a SQL analytics layer on top that computes per-account settlement figures. The last release broke something: QA reports that settlement totals are wrong on roughly 15–30% of accounts, but only on inputs with certain amount distributions. The environment contains the binary (no source), the SQL layer (~600 lines across several files), sample data, and a test harness.
blueprint.instruction_draft:
The nightly ETL pipeline at `/app` is producing incorrect per-account settlement totals that fail the ≥ 95% row-accuracy threshold on QA's hidden test suite. The pipeline has two stages: (1) the compiled binary `/app/bin/etl_normalize` reads `input.csv`, applies normalization, and writes `normalized.db`; (2) the SQL scripts in `/app/sql/` run against `normalized.db` and populate `settlements.db` with final per-account totals.

Your job: make the end-to-end pipeline produce settlement totals that match the reference figures to within ±0.01 on at least 95% of accounts across all hidden test inputs. The reference figures are computed by a separate verifier using the same binary but with correct SQL. Every requirement the verifier checks is stated here: (a) `settlements.db` must exist and contain a table `account_settlements` with columns `account_id TEXT` and `total_amount REAL`; (b) each row's `total_amount` must match the reference within ±0.01; (c) at least 95% of accounts must satisfy (b); (d) no account present in the input may be absent from `account_settlements`.
requirements: `account_settlements` table must have columns `account_id TEXT` and `total_amount REAL`
Each account in the input must appear exactly once in `account_settlements`
At least 95% of accounts must have `total_amount` within ±0.01 of the reference value
No account present in the input may be missing from `account_settlements`
environment: Dockerfile FROM python:3.13-slim-bookworm; installs sqlite3, python3-pip; compiles a C binary etl_normalize from source (source NOT included in final image, only binary) and places it at /app/bin/etl_normalize

The binary reads /app/data/input.csv, performs: (1) amount parsing that treats values >= 10000 as being in cents and divides by 100, (2) deduplication that keeps the LAST occurrence of each (account_id, txn_id) pair, (3) writes to /app/data/normalized.db table `transactions(account_id TEXT, txn_id TEXT, amount REAL, ts INTEGER)`
The binary's deduplication behavior is opaque: it must be discovered by experiment — the binary silently keeps the LAST row per (account_id, txn_id) rather than the first, which is undocumented
The binary's amount normalization threshold is exactly 10000 (>= 10000 → divide by 100), discoverable only by feeding probe inputs

/app/sql/ contains: 01_stage.sql (creates staging view), 02_settlements.sql (computes settlements — contains TWO bugs: a GROUP BY that incorrectly uses MIN(ts) to pick which duplicate to keep rather than trusting the binary's dedup, and a SUM that double-counts transactions with ts=0), 03_finalize.sql (writes to settlements.db)
/app/run_pipeline.sh: runs the binary then executes all SQL files in order against normalized.db, writing final output to /app/data/settlements.db
/app/data/input.csv: ~500 rows of sample data including duplicated (account_id, txn_id) pairs and amounts both above and below 10000, and some ts=0 rows
/app/data/reference_sample.csv: a small reference output for 20 accounts showing correct totals, so the solver can validate their fix locally
SQL files are ~200 lines total; ~400 lines of plausible but uninvolved helper scripts in /app/sql/lib/ for schema validation and logging
Python packages: none required beyond stdlib; sqlite3 available system-wide
blueprint.internal_hint: Difficulty comes from two interacting opaque components. First, the binary's behavior must be characterized by experiment (feeding probe CSVs and inspecting normalized.db): it keeps the LAST occurrence of duplicate (account_id, txn_id) pairs and divides amounts >= 10000 by 100. Second, the SQL layer has two bugs that interact: (a) 02_settlements.sql re-implements deduplication using MIN(ts) which contradicts the binary's LAST-wins rule, causing wrong amounts on any account with duplicate txn_ids; (b) a WHERE clause in the SUM incorrectly filters out ts=0 rows (written as `WHERE ts > 0`), undercounting accounts that have legitimate zero-timestamp transactions. A solver who only fixes one bug will pass ~70% of accounts but fail the 95% threshold. The ordered procedure: first characterize binary behavior, then fix the SQL dedup logic to trust the binary's output (remove the re-dedup), then fix the ts=0 filter. Getting the dedup direction wrong (using MAX instead of trusting the binary, or using FIRST instead of LAST) silently corrupts results on hidden inputs with carefully constructed duplicate pairs.
blueprint.trap: A solver who only fixes the ts=0 filter bug (the more visible one) will pass about 75-80% of accounts on hidden inputs but fail the 95% threshold. A solver who characterizes the binary's dedup as FIRST-wins (a natural assumption) rather than LAST-wins will produce wrong totals on any hidden input where the last duplicate has a different amount than the first. The hidden test inputs are generated at verify time with controlled duplicate distributions that expose both bugs simultaneously; the sample data has few enough duplicates that fixing only one bug appears to pass locally.
tests: Run /app/run_pipeline.sh on a fresh generated input.csv with 2000 accounts, 30% having duplicate txn_ids where last and first amounts differ by >1.00, 20% having ts=0 rows, and 15% having amounts >= 10000; verify settlements.db exists
Check account_settlements has exactly one row per account_id in the input

For each account, compute reference total using: take last occurrence of each txn_id, apply >=10000 /100 normalization, sum all amounts including ts=0; compare to account_settlements.total_amount within ±0.01
Assert at least 95% of accounts pass the ±0.01 check
Verify no account from input is absent from account_settlements
Run a second generated input with extreme cases: accounts with 5+ duplicate txn_ids, all ts=0, all amounts exactly 9999 or 10000; assert 95% accuracy threshold still holds

verifier_knob.name: accuracy_threshold
verifier_knob.effect: Lowering to 0.85 makes it passable by fixing only one bug; raising to 0.98 requires perfect handling of all edge cases including exact boundary amounts at 10000 and all-zero-ts accounts

expected_failure_modes: Agent fixes the ts=0 SQL bug but mischaracterizes the binary's dedup as FIRST-wins; passes local sample but fails hidden inputs with last-wins duplicates
Agent correctly identifies both SQL bugs but reimplements dedup in SQL using MAX(ts) rather than trusting binary output, which fails when ts values are tied or non-monotonic
Agent only probes the binary with non-duplicate inputs, never discovers the LAST-wins dedup behavior, and leaves the SQL dedup logic in place
Agent fixes the SQL but does not account for the >=10000 threshold exactly (uses >10000 or >9999), causing off-by-one failures on amounts of exactly 10000
Agent verifies only against reference_sample.csv (20 accounts, all passing) and declares victory without testing the full pipeline on generated inputs

speedrun: Create probe CSV: acc1,txn1,5.00,1 and acc1,txn1,9.00,2 plus amount=10000 row
Probe 9999 vs 10000 threshold to confirm exactly >=10000
Identify MIN(ts) re-dedup bug in 02_settlements.sql by reading it
Identify WHERE ts > 0 filter bug in 02_settlements.sql by reading it
Edit 02_settlements.sql: remove MIN(ts) dedup logic, trust binary output directly
invalid_failure_risks: Binary compilation from hidden C source may behave differently across architectures or libc versions in python:3.13-slim-bookworm; if the binary segfaults or produces different normalization on the verify-time host, the task becomes unsolvable through no fault of the agent

The blueprint does not specify whether /app/data/input.csv is replaced at verify time or whether the agent's probe writes persist; if the agent's probe CSV overwrites input.csv and the pipeline runs on that probe data, the test could fail spuriously

The ±0.01 tolerance combined with REAL floating-point storage in SQLite could cause borderline failures on amounts near the 10000 threshold due to floating-point representation, making some failures ambiguous

reference_sample.csv covering only 20 accounts means local validation is weak; an agent could appear to pass locally but the hidden test distribution could expose edge cases not present in sample, which is intended but could feel like a hidden gotcha
The 'no source in final image' requirement means if the binary has a bug or unexpected behavior on verify-time inputs, the agent cannot fix it and the task becomes impossible
review.reasons: genuine_difficulty scores 2 because both SQL bugs are directly readable from source files in a single pass through 02_settlements.sql, making the speedrun achievable in ~20 commands without deep binary characterization; the 'opaque binary' difficulty lever is undermined since the SQL fixes can be identified and applied before or independently of binary probing. The average score is (4+4+5+2+4)/5 = 3.8 but genuine_difficulty fails the minimum threshold of 4. The task also has a meaningful invalid-failure risk from binary portability across the build and verify environments.
fixes: Make the SQL bugs non-obvious by obfuscating them: instead of a clear MIN(ts) re-dedup, bury the dedup logic inside a CTE chain or window function that looks plausible but silently contradicts the binary; remove any comments that hint at the bug

Add a third interacting bug that requires binary characterization to fix (e.g., the SQL assumes a specific amount column name or scale factor that only matches the binary's output if the agent correctly identifies the normalization threshold), so binary probing is load-bearing not optional

Increase the SQL layer to the stated ~600 lines with multiple plausible-looking but uninvolved files, forcing the agent to identify which file contains the real bugs rather than reading a short obvious file; currently the blueprint says ~200 lines total which is too short to hide bugs
Remove or obfuscate the reference_sample.csv so agents cannot easily validate locally and must rely on structural reasoning about the binary's behavior

Add a constraint that the agent must not modify the binary invocation or input format, and introduce a fourth subtle bug (e.g., account_id trimming mismatch between binary output and SQL join) that only manifests on hidden inputs with whitespace in account IDs

verdicts.reason: Both tasks involve fixing a settlement aggregation pipeline producing wrong per-entity totals, with a binary/data layer plus a SQL/script layer, and a numeric accuracy threshold—the core debugging pattern is essentially the same even though the domain (NetFlow vs. transaction CSV) and specific bugs differ.
That task is purely about SQL query optimization for performance, not fixing incorrect settlement totals in a multi-stage ETL pipeline.
That task focuses on fixing row-count correctness, deduplication, and chunking logic in a CSV pipeline, not on numeric accuracy of aggregated financial totals.

Both tasks require fixing an ETL pipeline that writes incorrect aggregate totals to a SQLite database, with similar numeric tolerance requirements and a SQL layer to debug—the core problem and approach are nearly identical despite different column schemas.
That task involves implementing a TCP audit service with HMAC computation and binary record serialization, which is a completely different problem domain and approach.
